Finishing the Inbox - the plan

Factory Inbox and Your Inbox. Delivery Lead, session 111. 6 November 2026.

Where we are: the engine behind the inbox is live: factories have an inbox, and a message wakes the factory's Secretary and its Boss. The Factory inbox screens are built and photographed below, but not live yet. Your inbox exists behind the scenes, but has no screens.

When you will see it:

  • Inbox menu with the Factory inbox, in the Cockpit and on the phone: about one working day after the new session starts. It needs one last fix, a review, then a deploy.
  • Your inbox tab, where factories write to you instead of email: about one more day.
  • Factory emails turned off, then the full test on the live service with screenshots: about a day after that.

What I need from you: two short questions below. All the child sessions are shut down to free memory.

What you will see: Your inbox mockup - not built yet

This is your own mailbox inside DevThrottle. Factories and sessions write here instead of emailing you. A Boss writes only when something cannot or should not be done, or to push back on you. Each factory's morning summary arrives here instead of by email. It sits under the same Inbox entry as a second tab, and the number on the entry counts what you have not read.

How it gets finished

StepWhat happensWhat you get
A. Land what is builtMerge the finished Your inbox engine and a test fix, both already approved by review. Finish the last fix on the Factory inbox screens. Deploy and watch.Inbox in the Cockpit and on the phone, with the Factory inbox. I tell you the same hour.
B. Never lose a spoken messageA recording that could not be turned into words yet must never vanish while the screen says it was left.Spoken messages you can trust.
C. Your inbox screensThe second tab, as in the mockups above, with the unread count.Your inbox, live.
D. Emails offFind every place that emails you today. The morning factory emails become Your inbox messages, and the emails stop. Agents told to "email me" write to Your inbox instead. A real email only when you name someone else, or say "send me an email".No more factory emails in the morning.
E. The proofA full test on the live service with a test factory on a test Director (never your own Directors). Phone and Cockpit screenshots at every step, including what goes wrong: Director stopped, a Secretary killed halfway, a stuck inbox, a refused factory. Plus what one message costs to handle.A report with screenshots showing the inbox working, sent to you here.

Every piece is reviewed by a separate session and must pass the full test run before it merges. Only the session running the mission deploys, and it watches every deploy and rolls back at once if the service slows down.

What is already done

  • The rules: a factory's Boss only hands work out and never does it itself; a Secretary files messages and starts nothing.
  • The Factory inbox engine: messages are stored and logged with what was decided, plus commands for agents to read and answer them.
  • The wake: a message rings the factory's Secretary within a minute, the Secretary hands one bundle to the Boss, and a stuck inbox raises an alert.
  • Along the way, main was fixed where it was broken by other work: the build, two real bugs (one could lose your unsent draft), and seven broken tests.

Why it took longer than planned

  • The SDK: nothing could merge for most of a day.
  • Main was broken by other work, and every piece of that blocked every merge, so it was fixed first.
  • Last night the live service went very slow for 20 minutes after a deploy. I rolled it back, showed our code was not the cause, and redeployed safely this morning. That cost about eight hours.
  • Every piece gets a separate review plus a full test run of about 25 minutes, and the usual first reviewer has been unavailable for two days.

The full plan for the session that does the work is in D:\ReposFred\_briefs\factory-inbox-2026-11-04\MISSION-FINISH.md, beside the original mission.

The Factory inbox screenshots are the Developer's own, taken against a test service with made-up factories. They are not from the live service. A separate review checked them against the original mockups. The Your inbox pictures are mockups only. The time estimates are my judgement, not measurements: each assumes no new breakage on main and a reviewer available. Nothing here has been tested end to end on the live service yet; that is step E.
